query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: cabin_service_complaint_presence
per_column.rationale: This is the primary intervention lever named directly in the query ('eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints'). It is intervenable: an airline can act on service quality to reduce/eliminate such complaints, so setting this indicator to false is a legitimate counterfactual manipulation.

per_column.name: crew_attentiveness_deficit
per_column.rationale: Crew attentiveness is the core dimension of 'cabin service', so this is a granular component of the same treatment being intervened on, not a distinct common cause. It is settable via staffing/training, hence intervenable. It is implied by the query's reference to cabin-service complaints, not an independent confounder.

per_column.name: food_quality_complaint
per_column.rationale: Food & beverage service is a cabin-service sub-dimension, so this reads as another component of the treatment set used to locate the 'most common' complaints. It is not a common cause of the crew/cabin-service treatment; it does not cause the treatment, so it is not a confounder.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_complaint
per_column.rationale: Seat comfort is a physical-product attribute, not cabin service, and it does not cause cabin-service complaints. It is a parallel/competing cause of the outcome (a precision covariate) rather than a common cause of both treatment and outcome, so it fails the confounder test.

per_column.name: entertainment_system_complaint
per_column.rationale: Inflight entertainment is a separate product feature that independently affects Overall Rating but does not cause cabin-service complaints. It is a competing cause of the outcome, not a shared common cause, so it is not a valid confounder.

per_column.name: service_recovery_indicator
per_column.rationale: Service recovery is an airline response that occurs downstream of a service failure/complaint (complaint -> recovery -> rating). It lies on the causal path from the treatment to the outcome, so it is a mediator (and potentially a collider), not a common cause to be adjusted for.

per_column.name: cabin_class
per_column.rationale: Cabin class plausibly causes both the treatment (higher classes receive better staffing/attention, lowering complaint likelihood) and the outcome (higher classes report higher satisfaction), making it a genuine common cause that must be adjusted for. It is not mentioned in the query text. Note it largely duplicates the pre-existing 'Class' column, limiting its added value.

judge.rationale: The treatment side of the interventional claim is well served: an explicit, intervenable cabin-service-complaint indicator plus granular complaint components matching the query's 'eliminate the most common cabin-service complaints', all of which an airline can actually set/change. However, the confounder side is weak. Of the added columns, most are treatment components (crew/food complaints), competing outcome causes (seat/entertainment complaints, which are not common causes of the treatment), or a downstream mediator (service_recovery_indicator). Only cabin_class is a legitimate common cause of both treatment and outcome, and although it is a confounder NOT named in the query (satisfying the decisive test), it essentially re-derives the existing 'Class' column and stands alone. Obvious additional unnamed confounders that would gate the counterfactual (e.g., traveller type, route/region, airline, review era) were not added. So the intervention is set up, but the deconfounding needed to read off the counterfactual effect is thin.
